name: Worldbuild
identity_check: Confirmed as Worldbuild (worldbuild.vc), the thesis-driven early-stage firm founded by Sumeet Singh, a former a16z investor. The site's only description, 'a thesis-driven investment firm that partners with creative technologists', matches his 'Theses' Substack, which the site links to. His X post of 2026-05-06 announces 'Worldbuild I, a $30M fund', and Upstarts Media covered it the same day. SEC EDGAR full-text search returns a Form D for 'Worldbuild Ventures I, LP' at a Brooklyn, NY address (Delaware entity) and a Worldbuild-branded SF Compute SPV. A one-person (solo-GP) firm. Not World / Worldcoin's 'World Build' hackathon programme, not World Labs, and not the Seattle-area 'Wbuild'. The 'Worldbuild VC' / 'Worldbuild Ventures' wording appears only in the fund's legal name. Portfolio note: Aetherflux, named by Upstarts ('Aetherfux') and by Singh's post, renamed itself Cowboy Space Corporation in May 2026. aetherflux.com redirects to cowboyspace.com, and the Worldbuild site now lists 'Cowboy Space Corp'.

thesis_text.value: Solo-GP, thesis-driven firm backing 'creative technologists' at the earliest stages. It publishes research theses before investing and favours two paths: 'model economy' infrastructure that AI needs to improve (compute, data, energy, security, on-device AI hardware) and AI-native apps that invent new workflows rather than bolting AI onto old ones; recent theses add energy-efficient materials and chemistry.
thesis_text.snippet: companies that build what models need to get better—compute, training data, and infrastructure—or companies that discover work that’s only possible because of AI.

open_items: Only 2 rounds found where a fetched page names Worldbuild (Interfere seed Oct 2026; Flower Computer pre-seed Oct 2024), well short of the 8 required. It is a $30M solo-GP fund, and most of its deals are unannounced or announced without naming it. None is industrial or hardware.

Portfolio rounds checked that do not name Worldbuild: SF Compute $40M Series A (2025-11-26), Browserbase $40M Series B (2025-06-18), Cowboy Space (ex-Aetherflux) $275M Series B at $2B (2026-05-11; Index led; Worldbuild not among the investors named; the Business Wire release returned 403).

Fractal Power (Austin; homepage banner 'Fractal Power raises $7M'): its Ashby job posts say it is backed by 'Riot, Definition, and Worldbuild', but no page describing that round names its investors. Search hints from databases cite a ~$9.8M Form D (Feb 2026), not verified. Not recorded as a round.

No funding announcement found for Truffle (Deepshard), Spinor Energy, Armory Medical, Actual Computer, Athanor or Company Picnic (on F4's list but not on worldbuild.vc). F4's page for Truffle points to a different domain (itsalltruffles.com) than worldbuild.vc does (truffle.net).
Check size not stated anywhere. F4's '$250K–$2M' is labelled as its own estimate, so it is not recorded.
No application URL or form. The site offers only a mailto contact (not recorded) and an X link. Cold inbound is taken from Singh's post: 'If you’re building your world, I'd love to connect.'
No company LinkedIn page is linked from worldbuild.vc, and none was opened. Singh's personal LinkedIn showed up only in search results and is not linked from the firm's site, so it is not recorded.

portfolio_count_reported: the firm states no count. worldbuild.vc lists 11 companies (Oct 2026) and F4 shows 12 (adds Company Picnic). Upstarts says 'Four of Worldbuild’s portfolio are previously backed founders'.
requires_us_entity and Indian founders: not stated. Every portfolio company found appears to be US-based.

SEC: the EDGAR full-text search (User-Agent 'CapitalAtlas research') worked, but www.sec.gov refused the Form D documents themselves. So amounts sold, final close, the GP entity and related persons were not read. Fund I's first Form D was filed 2025-02-14 (Delaware LP, Brooklyn address). The SF Compute SPV Form D was filed 2025-11-19 (Claymont, DE address). Fund I close_date is the announcement date (2026-05-06).
LPs per Upstarts (not a schema field): Village Global co-founder Ben Casnocha, a top 20 university endowment and several multi-stage VC firms.
Interfere's HQ is unclear: the seed post says it is hiring in New York, while startups.gallery shows San Francisco. Left null. Flower Computer's HQ (F4: Brooklyn) is also left null.
The X post was read through the public api.fxtwitter.com mirror of the same post URL; x.com itself was not opened.
